ice-train-delay-prediction.title: ICE Train Delay Prediction — Machine Learning Forecasting Model
ice-train-delay-prediction.subtitle: Time-aware regression pipeline for forecasting Deutsche Bahn ICE arrival delays
ice-train-delay-prediction.description: A machine-learning forecasting study combining ICE operational records with historical weather data to predict delay minutes.
ice-train-delay-prediction.overview: An end-to-end machine-learning capstone that forecasts ICE train delays in minutes from Deutsche Bahn operational data and Open-Meteo weather observations. The study uses a leakage-safe, time-based evaluation across July–September 2024 and compares naive, linear, bagging and boosting models.
features: Automated acquisition and preparation of ICE operational records
Station-level integration with hourly historical weather data
Time-based train/test split that reflects real forecasting conditions
Comparison of linear, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost and LightGBM models
Operational-only versus weather-enriched ablation analysis
Reproducible nine-notebook workflow with saved model-selection reports

architecture.name: Data Acquisition
architecture.description: Downloads monthly Deutsche Bahn Parquet data and filters the workflow to ICE services.

architecture.name: Data Integration
architecture.description: Joins station and planned-departure records with hourly Open-Meteo observations.

architecture.name: Feature Pipeline
architecture.description: Cleans timestamps, engineers operational and weather features, and stores typed Parquet datasets.

architecture.name: Forecasting Layer
architecture.description: Benchmarks regularised linear models, Random Forest and gradient-boosting ensembles.

modules.name: Acquisition & Cleaning
modules.description: Builds consistent monthly ICE datasets and removes cancelled or unusable records.

modules.name: Weather Enrichment
modules.description: Geocodes stations and aligns railway observations with hourly weather.

modules.name: Model Benchmarking
modules.description: Evaluates baseline, linear, bagging and boosting models using mean absolute error.

modules.name: Final Pipeline Export
modules.description: Persists the selected XGBoost pipeline and machine-readable experiment summaries.

contributions: Built a reproducible data pipeline spanning 377,000+ train-stop observations.
Designed a time-based evaluation strategy to prevent future-data leakage.
Benchmarked multiple model families against transparent naive baselines.
Measured the incremental value of weather features through controlled ablation.
Documented research questions, model selection and limitations in reproducible notebooks.
challenges: Integrating large railway and weather datasets across station and time keys.
Preventing temporal leakage while retaining operationally useful features.
Interpreting why a robust naive median remained difficult to outperform.
outcomes: Selected XGBoost with weather as the strongest machine-learning model at 10.31 minutes MAE.
Established that summer weather offered only a small predictive improvement.
Produced an honest, reproducible benchmark in which the 9.48-minute naive median remained best overall.

forestguard.title: ForestGuard — Satellite-Based Deforestation Detection
forestguard.subtitle: AI-powered forest monitoring with Sentinel-2 imagery and U-Net segmentation
forestguard.description: A full-stack geospatial AI application that detects, compares and reports deforestation from multi-band satellite imagery.
forestguard.overview: ForestGuard is a local decision-support platform that applies a trained TensorFlow/Keras U-Net model to four-band Sentinel-2 GeoTIFFs. It calculates NDVI, segments deforestation per pixel, compares two observation dates and exports geospatial results and PDF reports.
features: Single-date deforestation segmentation and affected-area estimation
Two-date comparison for new, persistent and potentially recovered areas
NDVI, probability-map and binary-mask visualisation
GeoTIFF, PNG, JSON and PDF result exports
Strict raster, band, alignment and model-availability validation
Background analysis jobs with clear progress and failure states

architecture.name: Frontend
architecture.description: React, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS provide the upload, analysis and reporting workflow.

architecture.name: API Layer
architecture.description: FastAPI coordinates validation, inference, comparisons, background jobs and downloads.

architecture.name: AI Inference
architecture.description: A TensorFlow/Keras U-Net processes tiled 256×256 raster inputs and stitches pixel-level predictions.

architecture.name: Geospatial Processing
architecture.description: Raster services preserve spatial metadata, calculate NDVI and estimate affected land area.

modules.name: Raster Validation
modules.description: Rejects incompatible files and verifies bands, projection and spatial alignment.

modules.name: Prediction Service
modules.description: Preprocesses, tiles and stitches imagery for memory-efficient U-Net inference.

modules.name: Change Comparison
modules.description: Calculates NDVI change and distinguishes new, persistent and possible recovery areas.

modules.name: Report Generation
modules.description: Creates visual previews, geospatial outputs, JSON summaries and downloadable PDF reports.

contributions: Designed the end-to-end architecture across frontend, API and geospatial AI services.
Implemented model-backed segmentation without mocked production predictions.
Built single-date and aligned two-date analysis workflows.
Added explicit validation and honest failure states for invalid imagery or unavailable models.
Created 29 backend tests covering mathematics, raster logic, inference tiling and API behaviour.
challenges: Processing large geospatial rasters within practical memory limits.
Maintaining spatial correctness across two-date comparisons and area calculations.
Communicating model and dataset limitations without overstating scientific certainty.
outcomes: A working full-stack prototype for repeatable satellite-based forest monitoring.
Downloadable decision-support outputs that preserve geospatial context.
A tested, modular foundation for future cloud deployment and model improvement.

vital-guard.title: Vital Guard — IoT-Based Fall Detection and Alert System
vital-guard.subtitle: Wearable IoT device with automatic fall detection and real-time caregiver alerts
vital-guard.description: An IoT wearable that detects falls using ESP8266 and MPU6050, then sends real-time, GPS-located alerts to caregivers via Blynk.
vital-guard.overview: Vital Guard is a wearable IoT safety system that protects seniors and people with disabilities by automatically detecting falls and notifying caregivers in real time with the wearer's live location.
features: Automatic fall detection using threshold-based motion analysis
Real-time caregiver notifications via the Blynk IoT platform
Live GPS location tracking of the wearer
Emergency alerts triggered on detected falls
False-alarm cancellation to reduce unnecessary alerts
Hospital lookup support for nearby medical help

contributions: Designed the end-to-end IoT architecture across hardware and cloud.
Implemented a threshold-based fall-detection algorithm on the ESP8266.
Integrated MPU6050 motion sensing with GPS location tracking.
Developed real-time caregiver alerts through the Blynk platform.
Added a false-alarm cancellation mechanism to improve reliability.
Tested the device across simulated fall and motion scenarios.
challenges: Tuning motion thresholds to detect falls reliably while minimizing false positives.
Maintaining stable Wi-Fi connectivity and cloud communication on a low-power device.
Coordinating sensor readings, GPS and alerts in real time.
outcomes: A working wearable prototype that detects falls and alerts caregivers with live location.
Reduced false alarms through threshold tuning and a cancellation mechanism.
Completed as my Final Year Project, demonstrating end-to-end IoT engineering.

text-analysis-toolkit.title: Text Analysis Toolkit
text-analysis-toolkit.subtitle: Dependency-free Python toolkit for reusable text analysis and reporting
text-analysis-toolkit.description: A production-ready Python package for tokenisation, frequency analysis, sentiment scoring and structured report generation.
text-analysis-toolkit.overview: Text Analysis Toolkit is a modular Python package and optional FastAPI web application for analysing text without external core dependencies. It exposes reusable APIs and a CLI for tokenisation, n-grams, frequency statistics, lexicon-based sentiment and text or JSON reports.
features: Word and sentence tokenisation with punctuation and stopword controls
N-gram generation and configurable frequency analysis
Lexicon-based sentiment scoring with custom vocabulary support
Plain-text and JSON report generation
Command-line interface for files and inline text
Optional interactive FastAPI web interface

Implemented reusable text-processing and analysis interfaces.
Provided CLI and web entry points for different usage contexts.
Added sample datasets, comprehensive documentation and 46+ automated tests.
Designed report outputs suitable for both human review and downstream processing.

Designing consistent behaviour across API, CLI and web interfaces.
Making lexicon-based sentiment transparent and extensible.

video-anomaly-detection.title: Video Anomaly Detection using Transfer Learning & Fine-Tuning
video-anomaly-detection.subtitle: Deep-learning system for frame-level anomaly detection in surveillance video

Transfer learning from pretrained CNN models

Evaluation across multiple benchmark datasets
